commenti.body: Long Legs director Osgood Perkins did one of the most subtle ghost stories ever made called I Am the Pretty Thing That Lives in the House. Can't say I loved the film (probably benefit from a rewatch), but there was plenty of atmosphere and striking visuals.

gotta check out all the BBC ghost stories (whistle and ill come to you is amazing and on youtube). and the j-horrors (ju-on, ringu, pulse, retribution). Dead Silence is underrated from 2007. the recent oddity was interesting. if i think of any more ill lyk.
Another vote for the BBC Ghost Stories for Christmas. Whistle, A Warning to the Curious, The Treasure of Abbott Thomas, The Signalman, The Stalls of Barchester. It’s exactly what you’re looking for!
[removed]

Burnt Offerings (1976) is one my favorite neo-gothic horror films set at the Dunsmuir House in Oakland, CA

Cast is spectacular with Karen Black, Oliver Reed, Betty Davis with Eileen Heckart and Burgess Meredith in supporting roles. Easily one of the most all time disturbing scenes in horror in it

The Changeling (1980) is another Neo-gothic with a great performance from George C Scott. Very atmospheric with a deep overall story about dealing with loss

You should check out Dawn Breaks Behind the Eyes (2021). It‘s a European, gothic horror film, that is pretty multi layered and surreal with an interesting approach to ghosts. Also reminded me of Last Year in Marienbad. 

The film is more on the abstract/interpretive side, so it might not be for everyone, but if you do watch it, I suggest going in as blind as possible.

The Legend of Hell House (1973) is a pretty good, more obscure movie about a group investigating a haunted house. It takes place in the 1970s but definitely has a Gothic feel to it.

The Vincent Price movies based off of Poe stories are all great Gothic horror.  Some of the best stuff Rodger Corman directed IMO:

House of Usher (1960)

The Pit and the Pendulum (1961)

The Haunted Palace (1963)

The Raven (1963)

Masque of Red Death (1964)

Tomb of Ligeia (1964)

The Oblong Box (1969)


If you're open to monster movies (Dracula, Frankenstein, etc.), Hammer Productions has a ton of great, Gothic horror. Some of the best Gothic horror movies ever made.  Depending on how far you're willing to go back, the classic Universal stuff is always great as well.

I would recommended checking out ***Ghostwatch*** a 1992 BBC TV movie about a TV show doing a piece on Halloween night where they spend the night in a supposedly haunted house. It's quite similar to "Late Night with the Devil"... but good. I did not find Late Night with the Devil to be that great at all, but this movie that came 30 years early did the same premise way better.

It may seem a bit flashy but thats only because of the TV show aspect, the actual hauntings are very low key until the very end and it's genuinely scary at times (unlike the aforementioned film, imo).

you can rent the movie on Youtube, or watch for free with Youtube premium. 

as far as Gothic movies go I would highly recommended checking out the movies of 1940's producer auteur "Val Lewton". His most famous movie is "**Cat People**" is pretty solid but I found "**Ghost Ship**" to be my favorite with "**The Body Snatcher**" being a close second. All his movies are set-up to feel potentially supernatural but not all of them are. Some of them are though.

and one last movie is "***Dead of Night***" (1945) which is a British horror anthology. There are a total of 4 short stories and then a 5th story that happens in the framing of the film. It's very gothic and has at a couple classic ghost stories like you're asking for.

You might like HALF-LIGHT from 2006. Stars Demi Moore. Also a lighthouse. Which is kind of gothic in a way. It has a resemblance to WHAT LIES BENEATH, which you've probably watched. 

I would also recommend A SINGLE RIDER from 2017. Now, it's not gothic at all, and is a Korean film and takes place in the sunny climes of Australia. But it is a subtle ghost story, but in the way that FIELD OF DREAMS is a ghost story.
I really liked Carlos Enrique Taboada's *Even the Wind is Afraid* (Hasta el viento tiene miedo, 1968) and *The Book of Stone* (El libro de piedra, 1969). Atmospheric gothic horror movies from Mexico.

I'll hijack this modern suggestion with one of my favorites of the year so far, *Oddity*.

I'll also add *Seconds* as it is one of my favorites all time and endlessely rewatchable...for more of the classic haunted house feel, check out *Rebecca*(1940) and *Gaslight*(1944)

The follow up to The Uninvited, The Unseen, its very much in a similar vein. Apparently there's a collection of ghost story TV films made by the BBC I think. They apparently made these specials at christmas every year for a long time. They're apparently very good films in their own right.

So many great recommendations here, definitely the exact kind of things I’m looking for. Thanks to both of you, I’ve never heard of any of these.

As to the J-horror, I’ve seen all of those but Retribution but don’t really remember Ju-On, are the sequels good too?

Hilariously, I feel like the opposite of the general public in that Long Legs is the only Osgood Perkins movie I haven’t seen. I actually really enjoy the atmosphere of I am the Pretty Thing that Lives in the House but ultimately don’t think it’s a great movie. I really like The Blackcoat’s Daughter though that is I think is retitled February in some places.

Great suggestions, I love Seconds, Rebecca and Gaslight… three of my favourites. Never heard of Oddity or the Servant. Wait Until Dark has been on my watchlist for years so I’ll definitely check it out soon. 

Thanks for bringing some new things on my radar.

These are great movies. Though I need to rewatch Burnt Offerings as I saw it when my son was born years ago and I think being so sleep deprived made me miss it completely, couldnt really tell you much about it.

I’m up for some schlock. As part of the Criterion Channels Halloween stuff we just watched an Australian Satanic Panic movie (I am Australian and so it’s always surprising to find something I’ve never heard of) called Alison’s Birthday which was a, rather poor, rip off of Rosemary’s Baby but it starts with one heck of a schlocky Ouija board scene.
I’ll definitely check this out, thanks so much for a recommendation. Blown away by people’s recommendations here, so many things I’ve never heard of,

I’ve been meaning to see Legend of Hell House so it’s good to get a second opinion in support of it. 

I’m certainly not opposed to monster movies - seen a lot of the Hammers and all of the ‘canonical’ Universals but it’s not the feeling I’m looking for here. Good suggestions though.

I really enjoyed Ghostwatch, it has a verisimilitude that I respect. I’m a sucker for doing any sort of ‘mockumentary’ (for lack of a better word) in as authentic a manner as possible. I seem to recall the difference in the video quality between the studio and location segments quite clearly as you would see in a broadcast at the time. Probably because it was just done with the actual BBC equipment but I think you can feel that stuff.

Great solid recommendations otherwise, though I’ve seen some of his movies had never had the name Val Lawton mentioned so I’ll explore that rabbit hole. Thanks

I will check both of these out. Thanks.

As an Australian I do get excited when other cultures film here, curious how this works for me.
I’ve never even heard of the Unseen, will definitely check it out. Someone above has mentioned these BBC films as well so I’m excited to seek those out. Thanks.

Hope you like it!

You definitely need to check out "Personal Shopper" with Kristen Stewart. It's not exactly a horror story, but it has some tense moments, and seems to meet your criteria for being a ghost story in an unusual, more subtle way.

Regarding Japanese ghost stories, a must-see is Kwaidan (1964), which literally means Ghost Stories, as it’s an anthology movie with four separate tales. Mizoguchi’s Ugetsu is a masterpiece, well beyond the genre, but Kwaidan has some of the most impressive color photography of all times. Then there is the “cinéma du WTF” highlight, House (Hausu, 1978). 

There’s also a subgenre related to ghost stories, tales that are variations on An Occurrence on Owl Creek Bridge. There’s a French wordless adaptation that was retrospectively included as a Twilight Zone episode, plus stuff such as Carnival of Souls or Jacob’s Ladder.
